chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Malik ibn Atiyyah, from Abu Ubaydah, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him)

He said: In the book of Ali, Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him), [it is stated]: There are three traits whose possessor never dies until he has seen their evil consequences: aggression, severing ties with near relatives, and giving false testimony under oath, by which he proceeds to fight against Allah. Indeed, the act of obedience that brings the quickest reward is keeping ties with near relatives. A community may be sinners but they keep ties with each other and [as a result] their wealth grows and they thrive. Verily, [giving] false oaths and severing ties with near relatives ruins abodes, turning them into wastelands for their inhabitants, and removes mercy – and verily in the removal of mercy lies the severance of one’s lineage.
ai.seo_question: What are the three traits whose possessor never dies until seeing their evil consequences according to Imam Ali?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) transmits a saying from Imam Ali (peace be upon him) warning that aggression, severing kinship ties, and false oaths prolong life only to delay inevitable divine retribution. This narration underscores the unique efficacy of *silat al-rahim* (maintaining family ties) in accelerating spiritual reward and material prosperity, even for the sinful, while its absence leads to the erosion of mercy and lineage. The text reflects the Shia emphasis on familial bonds as a primary mechanism for sustaining divine grace (*rahma*) within the household.
